title: Suffice Exact Repository Observations for Developer Agents
subtitle: Separating generation identity retained state and complete delivery
abstract: Repository tools determine which project state a coding agent observes and how much work each observation costs. Cache-lookup microbenchmarks can omit generation admission, retained-state costs, output encoding, and consumer materialization. We present Suffice, a C++20/Python research resource that couples immutable generations, exact predicate and range identity, independently bounded retention, and validated response completion. In a controlled backend experiment, 100 fresh processes execute 4,840 requests whose ordered paths and complete bodies match an independent original-byte oracle. Binary responses reduce complete-session response bytes by 49.45-49.59% and measured service time by 44.43-53.23% across four nonempty workloads. An empty-output control increases bytes by 2.30% and shows no consistent timing advantage. A separately tested completed-read bridge exposes generation-scoped results through a model-callable interface. The contribution is an executable observation contract and auditable evaluation resource. Bridge latency, Gemma inference, token savings, and issue-resolution gains remain unmeasured.
